title: Dusk as a practice
hookLine: lamps lit, work put down, the family gathered

lines: THE DAY DOESN'T END; IT RUNS OUT.
cards: Your phone probably knows when the sun sets. Around dusk the screen goes a little warmer, a little dimmer, without you asking. Somebody decided our devices should notice the evening.
It's easy not to. A day can go straight from the last meeting to the commute to dinner to scrolling in bed, and never quite end; it just runs out.
Long before screens, Punjabi households had a way to make the evening a real turning point.

teach.h: SANDHIAA: THE SEAM OF DAY AND NIGHT.
teach.b: The old Punjabi word is sandhiaa. It comes from a root meaning a joining: the seam where day and night meet. In South Asia, households of more than one faith mark that seam.
Lamps are lit. Shoes come off.

teach.h: LAMPS LIT, SHOES OFF, WORK DOWN.
teach.b: Work is put down. Hindu neighbors keep sandhya prayers too, and in Punjabi homes, Sikh and Hindu, a small lamp at dusk has been an ordinary sight. For Sikhs, dusk is when Rehras is said.

teach.h: REHRAS IN THE EVENING, AFTER SUNSET.
teach.b: The Sikh code of conduct places it in the evening, after sunset. Notice how that's put. Not to the minute.
In the evening, as the light goes.
The Gurus questioned rituals kept for their own sake, and gurbani puts remembrance above outward observance. So the lamp isn't the prayer. It's a reminder that the prayer is due.
What makes dusk a practice, then, is the putting down. The shop shutter comes down. The laptop closes.
The family, or just you, gathers. The day is handed back. Sikh life asks for kirat karni, honest work, through the day, and sandhiaa is the moment that work is allowed to stop.
That's the gift of a seam. Without it, today bleeds into tonight and tonight into tomorrow, and nothing is ever finished. With it, the day can actually end.

how: Sikhs say Rehras Sahib in the evening, after sunset, and some households mark dusk by putting work down, lighting a lamp and gathering, though the remembrance, not the lamp, is the heart of it.

games.q: it's dusk and you're still answering work messages. by the Rehat Maryada's timing, when is Rehras said?
games.why: in the evening, after sunset: dusk as a practice lets the prayer mark the turn of the day, and the work be put down.

practice: Light a candle or a small lamp, or just switch on one warm light and turn off the overhead; if it isn't dusk yet, picture where that light will be tonight.

Look at it, and silently name one piece of today's work you're putting down, the email, the argument, the unfinished task, and set it on a shelf till morning. If you pray, you can say Waheguru once, and let the evening begin.

wordCard.voice: Sandhiaa. Dusk, the joining of day and night, when Sikhs say Rehras: lamps lit, work put down, the household gathered.

carryVoice: Your line: put the day down. Shoes off, work down, the lamp lit. See you tomorrow.
